content: Meridian call went well. They want 40 seats but their security team requires a full audit log of every data change before they sign. Renewal target is September 15.
If Meridian needs audit logs we should decide the database now. Mongo makes audit trails painful. I want to evaluate Postgres this week.
Heads up, Hollis filed a ticket. CSV export drops rows when a field contains a comma. Marked it high priority, they export every Friday.
Decision made. Ridgeline moves to Postgres. Main reason is the Meridian audit requirement, transactional audit tables are simple in Postgres and a nightmare in Mongo. I will write the migration plan.
Noted. Ridgeline database decision: Postgres, driven by the Meridian audit requirement. Mike owns the migration plan.
Told Meridian about the audit log commitment. They are happy. Their security contact is named Priya, she wants a demo of the audit trail before renewal.
Fixed workaround for the Hollis CSV bug, we quote fields with commas on export. Mike, permanent fix should land with the API rewrite.
Migration plan is two phases. Phase one, new writes go to Postgres with Mongo kept in sync. Phase two, backfill history and cut reads over. Target four weeks total.
Pricing change proposal: move from flat 99 per month to 12 per seat. Meridian at 40 seats becomes our biggest account. Need a decision before the renewal.
Reminder for everyone, our refund policy is 30 days full refund, no questions. Hollis asked and I confirmed it in writing.
Logged. Ridgeline refund policy: 30 days, full refund. Confirmed to Hollis by Emily.
Phase one of the Postgres migration is live. Dual writes running clean for 24 hours. Audit table records actor, action, before and after values.
Priya from Meridian saw the audit trail demo. Quote from her, this is exactly what our compliance team asked for. Renewal looking strong.
Started writing the onboarding doc for new customers. First section covers account setup, second covers the export feature since that is where tickets come from.
API rewrite scope: versioned endpoints, the permanent CSV fix Emily asked for, and rate limits. Postgres backfill runs this weekend.
New lead, a company called Fairbanks Supply, 15 seats. They asked whether we support single sign on. Mike, do we?
Not yet. SSO goes after the API rewrite. Tell Fairbanks Q4 honestly, do not promise a date.
Recorded. SSO is not supported yet, planned after the API rewrite, roughly Q4. Fairbanks Supply told Q4 with no committed date.
Hollis confirmed the CSV workaround holds. Keeping the ticket open until the permanent fix ships in the rewrite.
Backfill done. All reads on Postgres since this morning. Mongo is now read only, we turn it off in two weeks if nothing breaks.
Migration status: Ridgeline fully on Postgres, Mongo read only, shutdown planned in two weeks.
Pricing decision from our call: per seat at 12 approved, existing customers keep the flat plan for one more year. Meridian renewal will be quoted per seat.
Onboarding doc first draft done. Sarah, can you review the setup section before I send it to Fairbanks?
Reviewed the onboarding doc, looks good. Sent it to Fairbanks. They start a trial on July 1.
Permanent CSV export fix is merged. Emily, tell Hollis it ships with the next release on Monday.
Told Hollis, they are glad. Closing the ticket after the Monday release goes out.
Meridian renewal signed. 40 seats at 12 per seat, twelve month term, starts September 15. Biggest deal in Ridgeline history.
Recorded. Meridian renewed: 40 seats, 12 per seat, 12 months, effective September 15. Largest Ridgeline deal to date.
Release is out. CSV fix live, Mongo shutdown scheduled for July 6. Next up is the SSO design for Fairbanks and whoever asks next.
Hollis ticket closed. Also updated the onboarding doc with the new export behavior so the next customer never hits it.
